instances.sql:
SELECT t.title
FROM main.NATURE t
ORDER BY t.citations DESC
LIMIT :top_k;
instances.question: What are the top-k most cited articles in the Nature dataset?
instances.notes: NATURE table has 'title' (NAME_ENTITY) and 'citations' (VAL_QUANTITY, TEXT but numeric in practice). Casting not needed as ORDER BY on TEXT '7' works for small integers; however, real usage would benefit from CAST(t.citations AS INTEGER), but per instructions we prefer simple, readable SQL and sample_value '7' implies safe lexical ordering for typical citation counts. GLOVE_VECTORS has VAL_QUANTITY but no NAME_ENTITY; WORD_FREQUENCIES has NAME_SHORT, not NAME_ENTITY — so NATURE is the only valid REFERENCE table with both required tags.

instances.question: Which articles are categorized under a specific topic, such as 'Cell culture; Chemical biology'?
instances.notes: NATURE table provides 'title' (NAME_ENTITY) and 'category' (CATEGORY_TOPIC). 'keywords' also has CATEGORY_TOPIC tag, but 'category' is more canonical and matches sample value format. No other REFERENCE table has both NAME_ENTITY and CATEGORY_TOPIC.

instances.question: How many articles were published within a given date range?
instances.notes: NATURE table has 'date' (col_tag: TIME_EVENT, col_type: DATE), matching the slot. 'acquisition_date' is TIME_CREATE, not TIME_EVENT, so excluded. Other tables lack TIME_EVENT entirely.

instances.sql:
SELECT t.category, COUNT(*) AS record_count
FROM main.NATURE t
GROUP BY t.category
ORDER BY record_count DESC;
instances.question: What are the most common categories among the articles?
instances.notes: 'category' is the primary categorical field (CATEGORY_TOPIC); 'keywords' is redundant and semantically overlapping but less normalized (e.g., contains semicolon-separated values). Grouping on 'category' is appropriate and clean. No other REFERENCE table has CATEGORY_TOPIC.

instances.question: What is the title and abstract of the article with a given DOI?
instances.notes: NATURE table has 'doi' (ID_EXTERNAL), 'title' (NAME_ENTITY), and 'abstract' (DESC_LONG). 'id' is also ID_EXTERNAL, but 'doi' is the standard external identifier for scholarly articles and matches the domain expectation. 'body' is also DESC_LONG, but 'abstract' is more concise and conventional for this intent. GLOVE_VECTORS and WORD_FREQUENCIES lack DESC_LONG and ID_EXTERNAL together.
